title: Chiles Rellenos
subtitle: poblano peppers stuffed with cheese, battered and fried
excerpt: Chiles rellenos are large poblano chillies roasted until their skins blister, stuffed with melting cheese, then coated in a light egg batter and fried until golden. A simple tomato sauce poured around each pepper ties the dish together. This is a dish that rewards patience at each stage.
sourceNotes: Chiles rellenos are a cornerstone of Mexican home cooking, most closely associated with the state of Puebla. The dish evolved from colonial-era cooking that combined indigenous chillies with Spanish dairy and egg-batter techniques.

glossaryTerms.definition: A mild to medium-hot fresh chilli pepper from the state of Puebla in Mexico. When dried, it becomes an ancho chilli. Poblanos are large enough to stuff and hold their shape when roasted.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes about 1 hour 10 minutes from start to plate. There are three distinct stages: roasting and peeling the chillies, making the egg batter, and frying. Do not rush between them.

The egg batter must be used immediately after whipping. Fold the yolks in gently and fry within minutes, otherwise the batter collapses and loses its lift. Have the oil hot and the stuffed chillies ready before you start the batter.

items.prepNote: Oaxacan or mozzarella, cut into sticks

content.text: Roast the poblano chillies. Hold each one directly over a gas flame with tongs, turning every 30 seconds until the skin is evenly blistered and blackened all over. Alternatively, place them under a hot grill, turning occasionally, for about 10 minutes. Transfer the charred chillies to a bowl, cover tightly with cling film and leave to steam for 15 minutes. The skin will loosen.

Make the tomato sauce. Fry the diced onion in a small pan with 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and simmer for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly. Keep warm on a low heat.

Peel the chillies. Rub the blackened skin off each pepper under cold running water. Make a small slit down one side, then carefully remove the seeds and membrane with a teaspoon, keeping the chilli intact. Pat dry with kitchen paper.
Stuff each peeled poblano with the cheese, inserting it through the slit. Press the opening closed as best you can. Dust the outside of each stuffed chilli lightly in flour, patting off the excess.

Make the batter. Pour the egg whites into a clean bowl and whip with a hand mixer until they hold stiff peaks. Beat the yolks with a pinch of salt and 1 tablespoon of flour in a separate bowl until smooth. Fold the yolks gently into the whites in three additions, stopping while some white streaks remain.

Heat 3 cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat to about 180°C. Working one at a time, spoon a bed of batter into the oil, lay a stuffed chilli on top and spoon more batter over it to cover. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until golden on the base, then turn carefully and fry the other side. Drain on kitchen paper.
Spoon the tomato sauce onto warm plates and lay a fried chile relleno on top. Serve immediately while the cheese is still molten.

attrs.symptom: The batter slides off the chilli in the oil.
attrs.cause: The chilli was not dry enough, or the flour dusting was too thin.
attrs.fix: Pat the chillies very dry with kitchen paper and make sure the flour coating covers the whole surface before dipping in batter.

attrs.symptom: The cheese has leaked out into the oil.
attrs.cause: The slit was too long, or the cheese was not packed tightly enough inside.
attrs.fix: Press the slit closed with a cocktail stick before battering. Remove the stick after frying.

attrs.symptom: The batter is flat rather than light and puffy.
attrs.cause: The egg whites were not whipped to stiff peaks, or the batter sat too long before frying.
attrs.fix: Start frying within 2 minutes of folding the batter. Do not let it rest or it will deflate.

content.text: Chiles rellenos come from Puebla in central Mexico. They are a special-occasion dish that takes time and care. The
chilli is large and mild, which makes it suited to stuffing. Once you get the batter technique right, the results are impressive.
